body:
### Summary

Today, package caching is "all or nothing".

There are some setup's where a user would like to use caching for almost all packages, but force a re-download and build of a specific package every time. This may be due to build behaviors, lack of package metadata describing dependencies, and environment variable based build behaviors.

I would like to request an analogue to `--no-cache`: `--no-cache-package`, which disables read/write from/to the uv cache directory for the specified package(s) only. Having this exposed in both the CLI arguments and the `uv.toml`/`pyproject.toml` would allow easy management of specific package's caching behavoirs without having to construct chains of commands based on group / extra exclusions.

### Example

uv sync --no-cache-package theseus-ai
title: Support for `--no-cache-package` in `sync` and `run`
